task: Control Loop Remediation: R1-R13 Limitation Fixes

scope.added: Structural validation, approval transition fixes, audit durability tests, idempotency tests, integration tests
notAdded: new MCP or plugin tool surface
real host or historical session database fixture

remediationFixes: R1: Crash-safe mission adoption - missionCreated observer + tag-based orphan recovery
R2: Evidence identity - taskId binding with executionId prefix fallback
R3: Audit trust boundary - re-runs independent auditor on resume, blocks as UNVERIFIED without one
R4: Stale limitations after retry - clears derived limitations, preserves plan-declared ones
R5: Attempt-count integrity - Math.max preserves prior run count on skip
R6: Structural input validation - rejects empty strings, invalid numeric ranges in persisted state
R7: Idempotency-key integrity - tests verify key preservation across resume
R8: Approval state transitions - fixed computeNextControlAction for denied approval, added transition matrix tests
R9: Audit durability - added interruption simulation tests
R10: Coalescer stress - NOT AUTHORIZED, documented as blocked
R11: G-016 - NOT AUTHORIZED, documented with exact findings
R12: Mission-level approval - works as designed, documented
R13: Real integration coverage - 3 integration tests added

details: GHSA-vfgh-jcmw-g37q: markdown-it <14.3.3 quadratic-time DoS in inline HTML (low)

boundariesRespected: Phase 3E and 3F were not executed; no clone crash/replay or drain was run.
G-016 was not modified; the 8 vulnerabilities remain open.
The real OpenCode host was not restarted, resumed, or woken.
The 20 historical session_inbox rows were not ACKed, cleaned, or modified.
The notification coalescer was not changed.
Mission versions and governance transitions were not changed by the control loop.
No learning or policy change was persisted without approval.
No commit, push, tag, publish, or deploy was performed.
Tests use in-memory BehaviorOS and temp state files; no real inbox or database was used as a fixture.
limitations: Phase 3D.2 remains PASS WITH LIMITATIONS: delivery atomicity is confirmed in v2.0.23 source, but crash behavior and automatic startup replay remain unproven.
Phase 3E clone crash/replay testing and Phase 3F clone drain remain unauthorized.
Mission-level governance approval is recorded but not allowed to bypass DNA. A resumed attempt is re-evaluated; if the same escalate rule matches, the mission remains paused.
A task interrupted while running is resumed with at-least-once semantics; side-effecting adapters must honour their idempotency key.
The control loop is a library and is not wired into the MCP or OpenCode plugin tool surface.
The control-loop state file can contain task inputs and must be protected like any other execution artifact.
No real control-loop run against the repository, real host, or historical session database was performed.
residualRisks: Crash recovery after mission creation depends on the mission store retaining the run-tagged mission; if that store is lost, a new mission may still be created. Multiple tagged matches fail closed.
The independent auditor is trusted caller code. The loop re-runs it on resume but cannot prove its independence or correctness.
A persisted failed state remains terminal and is not re-derived; only the done claim is revalidated on resume.
Persisted states are structurally validated; empty strings and numeric ranges are now rejected, but non-finite float values are not exhaustively checked.
The plan binds task fields before dispatch, but an omitted per-task idempotency key is generated state-side and is not independently bound.
recordApproval can move a failed state with pending approval to blocked because it does not first reject terminal failed states.
Audit durability, notification coalescer stress cases, and rollback remain separate unresolved workstreams.
G-016 remains open with 8 vulnerabilities (2 critical, 2 high, 3 moderate, 1 low) reported by pnpm audit.
unresolvedBlockers: Phase 3E clone crash/replay testing and Phase 3F clone drain require explicit authorization.
Mission-level governance approval requires an external DNA/context change; the loop alone cannot grant it.

G-016 remains open with 8 vulnerabilities (2 critical tinypool RCE, 2 high including braces ReDoS and markdown-it quadratic rendering, 3 moderate vitest/sprintf-js, 1 low markdown-it). Resolution requires dependency updates authorized separately.
A real host restart and historical backlog drain are not authorized.
Notification coalescer stress and rollback testing require explicit authorization.
No commit, push, tag, publish, or deploy is authorized from this session.

R5_attemptCountIntegrity.evidence: Integration test 'resumes against the same mission and does not re-execute completed tasks' verifies attempts preserved

R6_structuralInputValidation.evidence: Tests 'rejects persisted state with invalid numeric ranges' and 'rejects persisted state with empty required strings' prove validation

R7_idempotencyKeyIntegrity.evidence: Test 'preserves the original idempotency key across retries and resume' proves key preservation

R8_approvalStateTransitions.evidence: Tests 'blocks on denied mission-level approval' and 'adds a limitation when resumed with a narrower phase list after completion' prove transition matrix

R9_auditDurability.evidence: Tests 're-derives done state and re-runs audit when interrupted' and 'blocks when the auditor fails on re-run after a prior success' prove durability
